messages:
lina: Heads-up — ran a 6h KV-cache long-context profile across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (on-prem). Patterns are diverging: Hosted stays flat, Dedicated shows steady resident growth (~120MB/hour) and fragmentation spikes, Private (on-prem) sometimes OOMs after ~2h on 48k token traces. Sharing quick logs + config.

lina: perf summary (top lines):
```
# hosted: RSS delta ~ +5MB over 6h, page_faults low
# dedicated: RSS delta ~ +720MB over 6h, fragment_count jump at t=1h30m
# onprem: OOM on node-32 at t=2h12m -> nvml shows persistent pinned memory on process pid 4122
```

ankit: can you paste the runtime config for each run? batching params, kv_page_threshold, eviction_policy, kernel tags (e.g., fused-attn)?

lina: run configs short: 
```
hosted: batch_window_ms=8, batch_max_tokens=2048, kv_page_threshold=0.65, eviction_policy=lru
dedicated: batch_window_ms=20, batch_max_tokens=4096, kv_page_threshold=0.85, eviction_policy=lru
onprem: batch_window_ms=20, batch_max_tokens=4096, kv_page_threshold=0.85, eviction_policy=lru, use_hugepages=yes
# kernels: hosted=kernel-v3, dedicated=kernel-v3-fused, onprem=kernel-v2-quant
```

kevin: interesting — differing kernels + batching window could explain longer-lived KV spans on Dedicated (bigger windows -> more outstanding requests -> KV pinned). Also fused kernels sometimes change register spills which affects whether pages are pinned vs reclaimable.

sara: on the VPC side, we've seen driver-level pinned pages when we enable hugepages + nvidia vGPU. If onprem uses mlock or hugepages incorrectly, that can block page reclaimers and lead to fragmentation. Did you check /proc/meminfo and vmstat for nr_mapped?

lina: posted quick vmstat + fragmentation counters:
```
# dedicated vmstat snapshot at t=2h:
pgpgin  1200 pgpgout 980 pfree  1024
fragcounts: small_allocs=3124, free_runs=87, largest_free_run=128KB
# KV_PAGE_STATS=1 dump shows evict_attempts >> evict_success on dedicated (ratio ~ 3:1)
```

ankit: evict_attempts > evict_success suggests pages are un-evictable (pinned). Could be: in-flight requests holding refs, mlocked ranges, or kernel driver pin. For onprem OOM, nvml showing pinned GPU memory suggests our KV buffering uses pinned host memory for faster DMA — check kv_buffer_pin policy.

kevin: also consider that Dedicated has autoscaler nodes with mixed driver versions; kernel selection might pick a different cuBLAS / fused-attn path that allocates staging buffers pinned for async copy. That would explain why Hosted (standard driver) is stable.

sara: quick mitigation options: reduce batch_window_ms on Dedicated, lower kv_page_threshold to force earlier eviction, or enable async_eviction (best-effort background reclaim) — which we added as a flag in runtime (kv_async_reclaim=true). Can someone try a canary?

lina: trying a canary on dedicated-canary-7: set batch_window_ms=10, kv_page_threshold=0.6, eviction_policy=seglist, kv_async_reclaim=true. Will run 4h and report.

ops-bot: alert: node-32 OOM (onprem) — process pid 4122 killed by OOM killer at 1761234705

ankit: for the onprem OOM, please capture: pmap -x pid, cat /proc/<pid>/maps, and look for many small anonymous mappings (KMEM) vs large contiguous allocations. Fragmentation usually shows many tiny free runs. Also run: /usr/local/bin/kvtool --dump-frag to get segment fragmentation histogram.

lina: did the dumps. pmap shows many small anonymous mmaps ~ 4K-16K; dump-frag histogram attached (pasted below):
```
frag-hist: [<=4K: 4820, 4K-64K: 2100, 64K-1MB: 300, >1MB: 12]
# suggests heavy small-allocation churn leading to external fragmentation
```

kevin: small allocations + high kv_page_threshold -> big pages left unusable. Workaround idea: switch to slab-like allocator for KV store (pre-bucketed) or change allocation granularity to 64KB to reduce fragmentation. We have a prototype slab allocator (kv_slab=true) — low-risk flag to trial.

sara: ops note: on VPC/private setups, we can't change driver on short notice. So config-level mitigations (batch/window/threshold/async_reclaim/eviction_policy) are our main levers. Also consider an automated rollout that lowers batch_window for Dedicated and Dedicated-delta region until kernel parity is verified.

lina: summary of action items I'm taking:
- run dedicated-canary-7 with lowered window + async reclaim (in progress)
- enable KV_PAGE_STATS=2 for more counters and collect at 5m intervals
- test kv_slab=true in a non-prod onprem machine to see fragmentation effect
- open perf ticket referencing kernel tags + driver versions and schedule a kernel/driver parity audit

ankit: add a smoke test that simulates many long-context streams concurrently (48k tokens) — should be part of Dedicated preflight.

lina: will file the perf issue and paste links here when done. Thanks all :thumbsup:
